author: lightclient
content:
okay taking a look. this fee mechanism kinda concerns me. it is trying to do a lot by having long running avg of registrations. but i dont really see the point of it because you can still register nearly 1m per day at the current rates, so a malicious actor could fairly cheaply register many millions of "fake" registrations before the fork. which is the whole point the fee tries to avoid. the real dos mechanism is the cost of the registration. it's already like 270k gas, probably no adversary would want to pay that much eth to just delay the registration queue a few hours

i would make the fee a smaller fixed fee, if at all, and remove the dynamic pre-fork fee calculation

author: potuz
content:
that sounds more complicated to me, to have a fee mechanism that changes pre/post fork, but I'm definitely talking out of my butt here, I'll trust whatever you think it's safe. The only constraints I have is that

- Assume that post fork the CL can consume Y preregs per block
- Pre fork, a spammer willing to spend X dollars should not be able to spam  more than Y prereg per block for a long time (say hours/days)
- Pre and post fork an honest party willing to pre-register should be able to pay very little to do so if they wait enough slots
